newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil heads Russian shares but demand seen low.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil heads Russian shares but demand seen low.

text.p: Russian oil company LUKoil led major Russian shares in morning trade on Friday, although traders said a brief spurt of demand had faded on most "blue chips" in favour of lesser known firms.
They saw prices flat at the close.
The Russian Trading System 22-share index drooped to 359.91 at 0900 GMT from 360.54 on Thursday.
"The market is following LUKoil," said Trinfiko trader Ilya Galtsov, citing low activity in leading shares. "Continued demand for LUKoil is keeping it fairly warm although it's not very agressive."
LUKoil posted net 1996 profit of 3.84 trillion roubles, up from 2.40 trillion roubles in 1995, on Thursday, and said oil production rose to 58.5 million tonnes from 57.3 million tonnes.
Russia's biggest oil company, said it planned higher investment in 1997, and would boost crude and oil products exports.
LUKoil edged up to $15.48 at 0950 GMT after closing on Thursday at $15.45. National power company UES firmed to $0.3140 at $0.3135.
National savings bank Sberbank, which traders said was one of this week's top performers, steamed higher to $197.00 from $187.00.
Sberbank was recently transferred from the second tier of the RTS system to the top level, reserved for the more liquid shares in some of Russia's premier companies.
But Brunswick trader Gary Kinsey said the second tier continued to absorb most funds, leaving top shares rangebound.
"Most of the focus is on smaller energy companies. The blue chip market is pretty dead," said Kinsey. "Volumes should be pretty light, there's no real interest today."
And Galtsov said it was unlikely the picture would change in the short term.
"Today it definitely won't change. I don't predict that the market will rise next week -- it's more likely it will stay at the same levels," he said.
